summary: Nightingale Health — sustained 5xx burst and streaming truncation during EU maintenance window; customer escalation and action plan
description:
Issue summary:
During the scheduled EU control-plane maintenance window (2026-03-10 11:45–12:30 UTC), Nightingale Health observed a sustained burst of 5xx errors and multiple streaming response truncations. Customer reported increased tail latency and truncated streams beginning ~11:50 UTC which persisted intermittently until mitigation at ~12:22 UTC. Impact: degraded user-facing inference (chat/streaming) and increased token billing for retries.

Impact:
- Customer-facing streaming truncation (partial transcripts) for ~32 minutes with ~18% request error rate for affected routes.
- Elevated 5xx (502/504) and gateway timeouts; some requests retried by client, amplifying load.
- Billing exposure due to client retries and duplicate partial completions.

Environment:
- Prod / eu-west-1 serving pool (dedicated nodes for Nightingale enterprise account).
- Models in use: open-llama-13b-v2 for chat; redwood-moderation-v1 for safety precheck.
- Rolling control-plane maintenance with coordinator update (scheduled but separate change to routing fallbacks).

Timeline (local UTC):
- 11:40: scheduled maintenance window begins (control-plane coordinator rolling update).
- 11:50: first customer report via support-email: "streaming truncated, repeated partial messages". Ticket auto-created.
- 11:52: Support opened #support-nightingale Slack thread and escalated to SRE.
- 11:55: SRE observed spike in 502/504 in eu-west serving gateway; routing fallback policy triggered but misclassified dedicated pool as unavailable.
- 12:05: Increased retries from client observed; request fanout increased load on dedicated pool.
- 12:15: SRE applied emergency circuit damping on routing layer to stop aggressive fanout to fallback pools.
- 12:22: Errors and truncations fall back to baseline; monitoring shows stabilization.
- 12:30: Maintenance window completes; post-checks run; customer notified.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Use Nightingale account with dedicated pool pinned.
2) During controlled routing coordinator restart, simulate a transient control-plane lag by delaying heartbeat acknowledgement on one coordinator for ~30–90s.
3) Send concurrent streaming chat requests with moderate retry/backoff disabled to observe fallback amplification and truncated streams.

Logs / Observations:
- Gateway logs (eu-west): repeated 502 upstream errors originating from serving-runtime health-check timeouts (sample log id=eu-west/20260310/11:56:24).
- Router audit: routing policy mis-evaluated dedicated pool state because heartbeats latched as "degraded" while KV prefix was still valid; fallback loop triggered additional multipath fanout.
- Observability: prefix cache size stable; CPU on dedicated nodes rose from 45% to 88% during peak, causing tokenization stalls and KV fetch delays.

Notes on customer communication:
- Customer was notified within first_response_due_at (11:58 UTC) and provided interim status updates every 8–10 minutes.
- Nightingale requested credits for duplicate partial completions; finance/cs to evaluate billing delta.
comments: Support (Aisha): Logged initial report and created incident ticket. Opened #support-nightingale and invited SRE and Eng. Notified customer of investigation and ETA for first update.

SRE (Liam O'Connor): Observed 502/504 spike tied to routing fallback during coordinator restart. Hypothesis: routing decision component marked dedicated pool degraded prematurely due to heartbeat lag; created INT-43120 to track root-cause in coordinator. Applied temporary damping on fallback decisions at 12:15 UTC.

Eng (Diego): Confirmed routing policy logic includes a conservative \"fail fast\" threshold that can be tripped by delayed heartbeats during rolling restarts. Preparing PR to add hysteresis and cross-check with KV cache staleness. PR posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821
Customer (Nightingale Ops, Maya R.): Appreciated rapid updates. Reported fewer truncated streams after 12:20 UTC; asked for formal post-incident notes and billing credit request steps.
Support (Aisha): Provided next steps and preliminary action items; escalated billing request to finance (ticket FIN-2026-045). Scheduled follow-up call for 2026-03-13.
SRE (Liam): Added monitoring alert to detect rapid fallback-amplification patterns and created a dashboard panel: /dashboards/fallback-amplification-eu-west. Linked in runbook.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Coordinator rolling update induced transient heartbeat latency -> routing policy marked dedicated pool degraded -> fallback routing amplified requests to mixed pools causing serving-runtime overload.
Hypothesis 2: KV cache staleness check not wired into fallback gating; routing decision only considered heartbeat, not prefix validity, leading to unnecessary multipath fanout.

Finding: Heap of evidence from router audit logs and coordinator traces indicate heartbeats for coordinator-3 were delayed by 8–24s during restart; routing decision logic used an immediacy threshold of 5s which was too tight for rollouts. KV cache remained valid, so fallback was unnecessary.

Telemetry: CPU and tail latency correlated with times when fallback decisions increased multipath fanout; tokenization stalls observed and internal retry counters spiked by 2100% for the Nightingale tenant during the peak window.

Related artifacts: INT-43120 (coordinator heartbeat root-cause), PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821 (hysteresis fix), Confluence runbook updated at /Incident+Runbook+EU+Maintenance+2026-03-10.
Mitigation tested: added 10s hysteresis and KV-validity gate in a staging cluster; replay of failure scenario did not trigger fallback amplification; streaming truncation not reproduced.
resolution: Mitigation applied during incident: emergency circuit damping on routing layer to reduce multipath fanout (12:15 UTC). This reduced load and allowed serving nodes to recover.

Post-incident fix: merged PR with routing hysteresis + KV-validity gating to prevent premature fallback (merged 2026-03-11). Deploy scheduled to eu-west during low-traffic window 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC (INT-43120 rollout).
Customer remediation: Support issued guidance to Nightingale devs to enable exponential backoff for client retries temporarily; offered to help validate retry configs in a staging workspace.
Billing: CS submitted billing review request to finance (FIN-2026-045) to estimate credits for duplicate partial completions; preliminary estimate pending (expected by 2026-03-16).
Monitoring / Alerts: New alert created to detect fallback-amplification patterns (threshold: multipath fanout > 3x baseline for >60s) and dashboard panel added.
postincident_action_items: ENG-1: Deploy routing hysteresis + KV gate to eu-west (owner: Diego) — scheduled 2026-03-14. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821
SRE-1: Add canary check in rolling coordinator restarts to validate heartbeat latency before toggling pool availability (owner: Liam) — planned before next maintenance window.
CS-1: Follow up with Nightingale on billing credits and provide detailed duplicate-completions export (owner: Aisha) — due 2026-03-16.
DOC-1: Update maintenance runbook to call out fallback hysteresis considerations and customer communication template (owner: Ops Docs) — due 2026-03-20.
QA-1: Add chaos test that simulates coordinator heartbeat delays to CI job for routing logic (owner: QA) — due 2026-03-28.
customer_impact_summary: Enterprise customer Nightingale Health experienced degraded streaming and increased 5xx rates for ~32 minutes during an EU control-plane rolling update. Impact limited to their dedicated eu-west pool; no data loss reported. Customer seeks billing credit for duplicate partial completions and a formal post-incident review.
next_steps: - Confirm deployment of PR and validate in eu-west canary on 2026-03-14.\n- CS to provide billing delta and proposed credit by 2026-03-16.\n- Conduct 30-min post-incident review with Nightingale on 2026-03-13 (scheduled).
